newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK January unemployment data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK January unemployment data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK data showing unemployment fell by a seasonally adjusted 67,800 in January while underlying average earnings rose 4.25 percent in year to December.
"It just confirms that the pace of growth in the economy is definitely picking up."

"The acceleration in the decline in unemployment is in line with the signs that overall in the fourth quarter of last year and the beginning of this year the economy is certainly growing at above trend pace."

STEWART ROBINSON, LOMBARD STREET RESEARCH "The suggestion (from the rise in average earnings) is that the falls in unemployment have been causing the labour market to tighten, and that is beginning to be reflected in rising wage demands and underlying cost pressures."
"We have now had several very strong (unemployment) falls in a row which forces us to believe momentum is building in the labour market."

"You would expect the introduction of the job seekers' allowance to have had an impact, but stripping that out it is clear the labour market is still tightening and that is reflected in higher average eanrings.
"That is why gilts have come off. A rise of 4.25 percent isn't in itself too bad, but the danger is that earnings pick up even further towards the end of the year."

"The labour market data are strong and while very unlikely to prompt a near-term tightening of policy, they will increase speculation that rates will have to be hiked immediately after the election. Indeed today's data may even force Prime Minister John Major's hand and lead to a March polling date.

"The worst news for the government and money markets is the acceleration in underlying average earnings. This has been the risk for some time with unemployment falling as quickly as it has been. Moreover, the pick-up to 4.25 percent reflects higher wages in both production and services."
